help.intro: The superlative names the top of a group. Its adverbial form — after a verb, or with sein — is am …-sten: Er läuft am schnellsten. Im Winter sind die Tage am kürzesten. Adjectives ending in -t, -d, -z, -s or -sch take -esten so that you can hear the ending (am ältesten, am kürzesten, am leichtesten) — with one famous exception, groß → am größten; short a/o/u adjectives take the umlaut as in the comparative (am größten, am wärmsten, am jüngsten); and the irregular four follow their comparatives: gut → besser → am besten, viel → mehr → am meisten, gern → lieber → am liebsten, hoch → höher → am höchsten. Before a noun the superlative takes der/die/das and an ending — der schnellste Zug, das größte Haus — which you meet here as chunks and build later in the course.
help.tips[0].title: am …-sten
help.tips[0].text: schnell → am schnellsten, klein → am kleinsten, schön → am schönsten. After -t/-d/-z/-s/-sch add -esten so the ending can be heard: am ältesten, am kürzesten, am weitesten, am leichtesten. Exception: groß → am größten (no extra e).
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: In summer the days are longest.
help.tips[0].check.q: Im Juli ist es hier am ____. (heiß)
help.tips[0].check.why: heiß ends in an s-sound (ß), so it takes -esten: am heißesten.
help.tips[1].title: The irregulars — and the umlaut
help.tips[1].text: gut → am besten, viel → am meisten, gern → am liebsten, hoch → am höchsten, nah → am nächsten. Umlaut: groß → am größten (note: not größesten), alt → am ältesten, jung → am jüngsten, warm → am wärmsten.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: I like tea best. That tastes best.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Who lives nearest? – Anna, just round the corner.
help.tips[1].check.why: gern is irregular: gern – lieber – am liebsten.
help.tips[2].title: Before a noun: der / die / das …-ste
help.tips[2].text: der schnellste Zug, die größte Stadt, das beste Restaurant. Use it as a chunk: Berlin ist die größte Stadt Deutschlands.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: That's the best ice cream in town.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
help.tips[2].trap: der schnellste carries an adjective ending. Copy the pattern; the endings come later in the course.
help.tips[2].check.why: Before a noun the superlative takes the article and an ending: die größte Stadt — and groß takes no extra e.
help.tips[3].title: Three steps, one ladder
help.tips[3].text: schnell – schneller – am schnellsten. gut – besser – am besten. gern – lieber – am liebsten. Always learn all three rungs together.
help.tips[3].check.why: gut is irregular all the way up the ladder: gut – besser – am besten.
help.remember[1]: gut–besser–am besten, gern–lieber–am liebsten: the two ladders you use most.
help.context.en: Which season do you like best? – Summer. The days are longest then and it's warmest. – I think autumn is the most beautiful. – And which city is the biggest in Germany? – Berlin, of course. But I like Hamburg best.
help.mistakes[0].why: gut is irregular: besser, am besten.
help.mistakes[1].why: alt takes an umlaut and -esten after -t.
help.mistakes[2].why: Before a noun use der/die/das + -ste, not am.
help.mistakes[3].why: groß is the exception to the -esten rule.
help.hook: Crown the winner of any comparison — am schnellsten, am liebsten, das beste Eis der Stadt.
help.recall.known: From "Komparativ": -er + als, the umlaut, and gut – besser.
help.recall.today: The top step: am …-sten, and der / die / das …-ste before a noun.
help.table.caption: Three steps
sentences[0].why: The superlative after sein is am + -sten: groß → am größten, with its umlaut.
sentences[1].english: In winter the days are shortest.
sentences[1].why: kurz → am kürzesten — umlaut, and an extra e after the z.
sentences[3].english: This ice cream tastes the best.
sentences[3].why: gut is irregular all the way: besser, am besten.
sentences[4].english: I like drinking water the most.
sentences[4].why: gern's superlative is am liebsten — the top of gern/lieber/am liebsten.
sentences[5].why: hoch → am höchsten — the c changes place: höch-.
sentences[6].english: My grandpa is the oldest in the family.
sentences[6].why: alt → am ältesten — umlaut plus the -esten after t.
sentences[8].why: After -t the superlative takes -esten: am leichtesten.
sentences[9].english: He eats the most of all.
sentences[9].why: viel is irregular: mehr, am meisten.
sentences[10].english: Of all the cinemas this one is the furthest away.
sentences[10].why: weit → am weitesten — the -esten after t.
sentences[12].why: No umlaut on two-syllable stems: am langsamsten.
sentences[13].english: The sofa is the most comfortable.
sentences[13].why: bequem + -sten = am bequemsten — plain, no umlaut.
sentences[14].why: nah is irregular: näher, am nächsten — an h → ch switch.
sentences[15].english: That's the best ice cream in town.
sentences[15].why: Before a noun the superlative drops am and takes an adjective ending: das beste Eis.
sentences[16].english: Which of you lives the closest?
sentences[16].why: nah → am nächsten — the irregular superlative again.
sentences[17].english: My oldest brother is already fifty.
sentences[17].why: Before a noun: ältest- plus the adjective ending — mein ältester Bruder.
sentences[18].english: Best of all I like cycling to work.
sentences[18].why: gern → am liebsten — the preference superlative.
